correctness.rationale: For all finite fields and both matrix dimensions at least two, the two decompositions of a rank-one matrix W=(u+x)(v+y)^T give x_A x_C x_D x_B=x_A x_D x_C x_B, proving every pair of independent rank-one increments commutes; shared-factor pairs commute directly. Coordinate decomposition shows the rank-one triangle-presentation is precisely the matrix additive group, so every closed triangle edge path contracts. Direct rank-one neighborhood counting gives V,E,F and hence free integral H2 of rank V-E+F-1. Hurewicz and Whitehead complete an unrestricted integral wedge proof. Four independent prime-field mod-two boundary computations corroborate counts and homology, without substituting for proof.

evidence: The 2026 first-homology classification for strongly regular graphs concerns coefficient-field homology and only diameter-two graphs, rather than all matrix dimensions and integral simple connectivity.
The 2026 second-girth paper establishes g2=3 for Johnson and g2=4 for Hamming graphs; bilinear-forms graphs are a distinct rank-distance family.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A vanishing first-homology theorem, even for every coefficient field, does not imply trivial fundamental group or a two-sphere wedge. Neither the restricted strongly regular scope nor Johnson/Hamming family formulas imply the claimed all-dimensional result.

evidence: arXiv:2610.33869v1, abstract and Section 8: the families treated are Johnson, Hamming, folded Johnson and hypercube variants.
arXiv:2606.27328, abstract and Theorem 8.4: a classification of when first clique homology may fail to vanish for strongly regular graphs, not of integral homotopy types.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claim needs a nonabelian edge-path presentation showing all rank-one increments commute and that no kernel survives evaluation, together with all-parameter face counts and Whitehead. None of the inspected statements supplies these implications; first-homology vanishing alone is insufficient.

evidence: Burkey–Martin–Oulon (arXiv:2610.33869v1), introduction and Sections 5–8, formulate triangle-filling as second girth, and address Johnson/Hamming/folded families but not bilinear forms.
Cioabă–Mim (arXiv:2606.27328), abstract, introduction, Sections 7–9, and document search contain no named bilinear-forms family.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent descriptions would be nullity of every rank-one matrix Cayley loop under elementary triangle moves, a simply connected two-skeleton, or Lewis second girth three plus an explicit Euler-characteristic wedge rank. The inspected papers supply none for all bilinear-forms parameters.

evidence: Terwilliger–Williford (arXiv:2512.12125) studies distance partitions and subconstituent modules of bilinear-forms graphs, not triangle-filled topology.
Gavrilyuk–Koolen (arXiv:1511.09435) identifies the rank-one matrix adjacency model, not a homotopy-type table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Known distance-regular parameter and intersection-array tables determine graph valency and local triangle counts but do not determine simple connectivity, integral 2-homology, or a wedge decomposition. No exact matching homotopy table was identified.

originality.rationale: Full-text inspected 2026 Lewis-girth paper treats Johnson/Hamming/folded families, not the bilinear-forms rank-one graph. Strongly regular clique-field-homology results are neither all-parameter nor π1/homotopy classifications. No equivalence or dominating theorem found in targeted source research. Incomplete older source text and unindexed rank-one geometric-topology literature remain residual risks.
residual_risks: A differently named older rank-one incidence-complex simple-connectivity theorem may imply the first part; no such exact implication was identified.
The complete text of arXiv:2508.05871 was not accessible in the inspected representation; abstract alone cannot exclude every result in it.
Some geometric-combinatorial publications may not be discoverable in searchable indexes; this is not a uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The recently studied Lewis invariant distinguishes Johnson and Hamming distance-regular graphs. This result settles a separate central matrix-rank distance-regular family at the triangle threshold, with a constructive noncommutative-to-additive edge-path reduction and exact integral homotopy ranks for every prime power and matrix dimension. This goes beyond field homology, isolated computations, and routine parameter substitution.
